# Cops 'raid CPB office'
[](https://x.com/intent/tweet?text=Cops%20%27raid%20CPB%20office%27&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thedailystar.net%2Fbackpage%2Fcops-raid-cpb-office-1498846) [](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thedailystar.net%2Fbackpage%2Fcops-raid-cpb-office-1498846) [](https://www.linkedin.com/shareArticle?mini=true&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.thedailystar.net%2Fbackpage%2Fcops-raid-cpb-office-1498846&title=Cops%20%27raid%20CPB%20office%27)

...

Minutes before the beginning of yesterday's countrywide hartal called by the left-leaning parties protesting the power tariff hike, police allegedly raided the office of Communist Party of Bangladesh and picked up 11 of its leaders and activists. The detainees were later freed.
[Tap here to add The Daily Star as a trusted source google-preferred-source-badge](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=thedailystar.net) Police also lobbed at least four teargas canisters inside the office in Paltan around 5:30am, the CPB alleged in a press statement. Around 6:00am, police dispersed the protesters when they were trying to gather near Shahbagh intersection. They used noise emitting devices to disperse them.
Maruf Hossain Sorder, deputy commissioner (Ramna division) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, told The Daily Star that the devices were used to “bring the situation under control”. The half-day hartal ended yesterday with no major incidents of violence. Vehicular movement was normal in the capital and elsewhere. Police did not let the pro-hartal activists take to the streets in many areas.
Meanwhile, at least 12 people were injured as police swooped on a pro-hartal rally at a level crossing in Gaibandha town around 11:00am, reports our district correspondent. The CPB and its allies will hold nationwide demonstrations today in protest of the CPB office raid. CPB, Bangladesher Samajtantrik Dal and other left-leaning parties called the hartal after the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission on November 23 raised the power tariff by 5.3 percent.
The BNP also supported the hartal. Mahmudul Haque, officer-in-charge of Paltan Police Station, told this correspondent that police did not conduct any raid in the CPB office. Police picked up 11 people as they were trying to block the road in front of the CPB office, but they were later freed, he added.

# Bangladesh, Malaysia begin FTA talks, target deal by 2027
Photo : PID
DHAKA, Oct 27, 2026 (BSS) - Bangladesh and Malaysia today formally began negotiations on a Free Trade Agreement (FTA), aiming to conclude a modern, balanced and mutually beneficial deal by 2027 to expand bilateral trade and investment and strengthen economic partnership.

...

Head of the 31-member Malaysian delegation and Malaysia’s Chief Negotiator Dr Rashidi Said, and Bangladesh’s Chief Negotiator and Additional Secretary to the Ministry of Commerce Khadija Nazneen, along with senior officials from both countries, attended the inaugural session.
The two sides signed the Terms of Reference (ToR) to establish the framework and scope of the negotiations.
The commerce secretary said Bangladesh-Malaysia relations had been strengthened by historical friendship and shared cultural and religious values.

...

He said the issue of concluding a sustainable and mutually beneficial FTA by 2027 was discussed during Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s visit to Malaysia in June this year, when he met Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.
The first round of formal negotiations has now initiated the institutional process to translate that commitment into reality, he added.
The commerce secretary said an FTA was particularly important for Bangladesh to address the challenges of graduation from the Least Developed Country (LDC) category and maintain its competitiveness in international markets.
Located at the crossroads of South and Southeast Asia, Bangladesh offers promising opportunities for Malaysian investors, particularly in the halal industry, semiconductor skills development, digital trade, logistics and joint investment in special economic zones, he said.
He also expressed gratitude to Malaysia for supporting Bangladesh’s aspiration to join the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), a regional economic bloc.

...

According to him, bilateral trade between Bangladesh and Malaysia stood at around US$2.84 billion in 2025.
The agreement, once implemented, would create new opportunities for expanding trade, promoting industrialisation and boosting investment, he said.
Dr Rashidi expressed optimism that the negotiations could be completed by 2027 through mutual understanding, flexibility and a practical roadmap.
He also hoped that the upcoming visit of the Malaysian prime minister to Bangladesh would add further momentum to the process.
Bangladesh’s Chief Negotiator Khadija Nazneen said the FTA would facilitate market access, reduce trade barriers and create new opportunities for investment and employment in both countries.
It would also make trade procedures more transparent, simpler and predictable, she added.

...

The first round of Bangladesh-Malaysia FTA negotiations will continue until October 29.

# CPB office 'attacked' over Awami League links
## Two Jubo Union members reportedly injured; police deny attack.
**TBS Report**
27 October, 2026, 01:25 am
Last modified: 27 October, 2026, 01:27 am
Photo: TBS
**Local BNP, Jubo Dal and Chhatra Dal leaders and activists have been accused of attacking the Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) office in the capital's Purana Paltan, allegedly branding the party and its allies as Awami League supporters.**
The incident triggered tension and a clash last night (26 October), with Chhatra Union and Jubo Union leaders claiming that two Jubo Union members were injured and taken away by police.
However, Paltan Police Station Officer-in-Charge Ariful Alam denied that an attack or injuries had occurred. He said tension prevailed at the scene and police were present.

### [The Business Standard Google News Keep updated, follow The Business Standard's Google news channel](https://news.google.com/publications/CAAqBwgKMIivlQsw2ZKrAw?ceid=US:en&oc=3)
Around 10:30pm, Bangladesh Chhatra Union Central President Mahir Shahriar said their office had come under attack. He said they believed the attackers were local BNP activists and alleged that members of Paltan thana BNP and its affiliated organisations might also have been involved.
Mahir alleged that the attackers were trying to portray them as Awami League supporters. He said he, other central leaders of Chhatra Union, and members of affiliated and sister organisations were inside the office at the time.
At 11:10pm, CPB General Secretary Abdullah Al Kafi said he was heading to the office after learning about the incident.
"A mob party comes to a party office and attacks it. That is all I know so far," he said.
Earlier on Monday, police detained former Bangladesh Chhatra Union president Dipak Shil during a protest in Dhanmondi-27 against the obstruction of female Baul singers from performing in Sunamganj.
Cultural activists gathered in front of Meena Bazar around 4pm for a human chain, but police prevented them from proceeding with the programme. Participants said Dipak was detained at the scene.
He was released around 9pm. After his release, Chhatra Union and Jubo Union activists brought out a celebratory procession in Purana Paltan.
They alleged that Jatiyatabadi Swechchhasebak Dal activists attacked a gathering following the procession and that the confrontation later spread to the CPB office.
The CPB office occupies the sixth and seventh floors of Muktibhaban in Purana Paltan, while the offices of Chhatra Union and Jubo Union are on the eighth floor.
Around 10:30pm, Chhatra Union leaders said they were inside their office when the incident occurred. They alleged that two Jubo Union members were injured in the clash and taken away by police.
